fixes.explanation: You've got it, friend. “When Israel became stronger, they pressed the Canaanites into forced labor, but they never drove them out completely.” (Judges 1:28) Israel grew stronger, and the Canaanites were put to work. The verse also says they never drove them out completely.

That's it, friend! Judges 1:23 says they sent spies to Bethel, which used to be called Luz. Spies are the folks you send before an attack. And the very next verse has those spies spotting a man coming out of the city.
Messengers is a fair thought, baker, but the verse uses a different word. Judges 1:23 says they sent spies to Bethel. Same trip, different job title.

Reasonable guess, but the king never comes up in this scene. The spies ask the man, “Please show us how to get into the city, and we will treat you kindly.” (Judges 1:24) That's the whole request: the way in, with a promise of kindness attached.

Right, baker. Judges 1:25 says they put the city to the sword “…but released that man and all his family.” He showed them the entrance, and he and his family were released. That's the kindness the spies promised back in verse 24.

I see the thinking, baker, but that's not what the verse says. Judges 1:28 says that when Israel became stronger, they pressed the Canaanites into forced labor, “…but they never drove them out completely.” So the Canaanites were put to work, and not every last one was driven out.

You caught it, baker. Judges 1:35 says, “But when the house of Joseph grew in strength, they pressed the Amorites into forced labor.” The house of Joseph got stronger, and the Amorites were put to forced labor. Nothing in the verse says they were driven out.

That's right, friend. The angel says the people of the land “…will be thorns in your sides…” (Judges 2:3) A thorn in your side is something that keeps bothering you. Nobody wants one, and that's the word the angel picks.

A shield protects you, friend, and this is the opposite. The angel says, “…and their gods will be a snare to you.” (Judges 2:3) A snare is a trap, so those gods are something to get caught in, not something to hide behind.
Blessing sounds good, baker, but it isn't the word the angel uses. The line reads, “…and their gods will be a snare to you.” (Judges 2:3) A snare is a trap, something you can get caught in.

I'd love a cheer here too, baker, but the text goes another way. When the angel finished speaking to all the Israelites, “…the people lifted up their voices and wept.” (Judges 2:4) I think this one is heavy. They raised their voices, and what came out was weeping.

A stone is a fair guess, friend, but this verse doesn't mention one. Judges 2:5 says, “So they called that place Bochim and offered sacrifices there to the LORD.” They named the place, and they offered sacrifices to the LORD there.

Trumpets make a fun guess, baker, but they aren't in this verse. Judges 2:5 says they called the place Bochim and “…offered sacrifices there to the LORD.” That's what the people did there. The verse doesn't mention any trumpets.
